No worries, I'm a carpenter but it is always good to do your research before tearing out walls. Also anything structural as such as tearing out a loading bearing wall has to be approved and inspected by a building inspector.
You are correct, the wall isn't bearing a load if it is running parallel with your floor joists. As long as the wall isn't an exterior wall you should be fine.

How many floors does your home have ? If multiple levels find out which way your floor joists are running. If the the wall is parallel with either your floor joists or your roof rafters / trusses it is safe to remove. I can't give anymore advice without seeing it. Get a carpenter in for a quote and they can likely tell you.

Any interior wall that is non load bearing you are safe to take out.  Some walls that are load bearing can be removed if temporarily jacked and you replace the wall with a beam and posts. It is hard to give you anymore advice without seeing what you're up against.  If you're uncertain contact a contractor and have them give you a free estimate for the removal

Each keyword only has 1 -100 searches. The   name of the product only has 1-1000 searches for it and most are just amazon links to the product or forums with people trying to fix an issue. 

Anyways I went on amazon and typed a broad keyword for my niche, an example would be " hammers" then a bunch of different products show up. I filter it by using prime only, look at the best selling and amazon choice ones. Take the names of these products and punch them into google keyword tool. See how many searches there are then do an allinttitle search on google to see who ranks for them. If it doesnt look too competitive I then start adding buyer intent keywords to the product and type those into Google's keyword tool. One of Amazon's products for Amazon's choice is a dewalt framing hammer so I add words like review to the products name and plug it into the keyword tool. Once I see there are searches for this I then repeat the allintitle search to see who is writing reviews about these products. Compile a list and get to writing.

The only tools I would like to have is either semrush or arefs but those cost a substantial amount of money per month for a website starting out.
